ancient-sites-and-mysteries.summary: 2 site(s) in Yucatán: Chichén Itzá and the Sacred Cenote, Yucatán cenotes. Facts from official sources; lore labelled as claims.

laws.rule: Yucatán's state regulation on cenotes, caves and grottoes bans applying tanning lotions, soaps or other products that can harm the ecosystem in the three hours before entering or swimming in a cenote; biodegradable organic products are allowed only at bathing sites, where a shower before entry is required.
laws.heading: Reglamento de la Ley de Protección al Medio Ambiente del Estado de Yucatán en materia de cenotes, cuevas y grutas

laws.rule: Under Article 6 of the Yucatán cenote, cave and grotto regulation (Decreto 193/2014, last reformed 26 January 2017), anyone entering a cenote, cave or grotto must not take drugs or alcohol inside or enter under their effects, must not smoke, eat or drink inside, must not damage the site, its plants or animals, must not leave rubbish, run or jump inside, or relieve themselves in the water. Where a site runs as a swimming spot, a rinse shower is required before entering. Article 20 bans tourist use of a cenote that is highly contaminated or dangerous to reach. Sites run as swimming spots must have at least one lifeguard and life jackets for hire (Article 19). The sunscreen rule is recorded separately.
laws.penalty_signal: minor breaches 10 to 1,000 UMA (units of measure and update); serious breaches 1,000 to 50,000 UMA, plus closure of the activity (the regulation's sanctions article). The UMA value changes each year and is not stated in the regulation.

laws.rule: Ria Celestun Biosphere Reserve: CONANP's visitor rules say follow the management programme, don't disturb wildlife, get no closer than 50 m to flamingo populations, don't litter, don't camp outside authorised sites, don't introduce exotic species, don't cut trees, don't burn, and follow the authorities' advice.

Exempt: older adults, pensioners and retirees, people with disability and children under 12 (credential shown on entry). 75% off for students and teachers with a credential; 50% off for Mexican nationals and foreign residents who show an official document. Open 8:00 to 17:00.
